about: Campaign Mode's situation cards (docs/CAMPAIGN-MODE.md section 6): 1 to 3 interrupt each End Week. {place} is where the card happens (the week's rally or tour stop), {candidate} the candidate's short name, {target} the staffer or stakeholder involved. Every choice has the You get / It costs / Risk preview; 'fail' is a hidden chance, 'trace' a hidden trace weight. Cards with a trigger are made by the engine: exposure, poach, lawsuit.

situations.text: A heatwave hits on the day of the {place} rally.

choices.label: Go ahead anyway
choices.receipt: The rally went ahead. Small, sweaty, loyal. +1 in {place}.

fail.receipt: Twelve people came. One fainted. -1 in {place}.

choices.label: Move it indoors
choices.receipt: Air conditioning wins elections. +1.5 in {place}.

choices.label: Cancel, hand out water
choices.receipt: The water stand got {candidate} on the local news. +1 in {place}.

situations.text: A reporter ambushes {candidate} about a donor.

choices.label: Answer honestly
choices.receipt: {candidate} answered straight. Boring clip. Good boring.

choices.label: Dodge the question
choices.receipt: Dodged. The reporter wrote "declined to answer" in a very large font.

choices.label: Blame a staffer
choices.receipt: Theo took the blame. Theo will remember.

situations.text: The 7 train is down and your volunteers are stranded in {place}.

choices.label: Pay for cabs
choices.receipt: Cabs everywhere. The doors got knocked. +1 in {place}.

choices.label: Cancel canvassing
choices.receipt: A lost day in {place}. The Mayor's volunteers waved from a bus.

choices.label: Ask your crew for rides
choices.receipt: Your crew drove volunteers all afternoon. +1.5 in {place}.

fail.receipt: Two cars showed up. One was a scooter.

situations.text: Papa-Dani promises something {candidate} actually agrees with.

choices.label: Praise him
choices.receipt: "Good idea, Mr. Mayor." Voters liked the class. So did he.

choices.label: Stay quiet
choices.receipt: {candidate} said nothing. The news cycle moved on.

choices.label: Call it a stunt
choices.receipt: "A stunt." It landed. -1 for the Mayor.

situations.text: A staffer brings proof that one of the Mayor's aides lied about a contract.

choices.label: Use it now
choices.receipt: The story ran. The aide resigned to "spend time with his ribbons." -2 for the Mayor.

fail.receipt: The "proof" was a parking receipt. -2 for {candidate}.

choices.label: Verify it first
choices.receipt: Priya checked it. It's real, and it's ammunition for the debate.

choices.label: Refuse to use it
choices.cost: A weapon left on the table
choices.receipt: You put it in a drawer. Your conscience slept well.

situations.text: {candidate} is photographed eating pizza with a fork in {place}.

choices.label: Own it: "I'm a fork person"
choices.receipt: "I'm a fork person." Bold. Strangely respected.

choices.label: Fold a slice on camera
choices.cost: C$500 for the slice photo op
choices.receipt: A perfect fold. The fork is forgotten. Mostly.

choices.label: Say the fork was ironic
choices.receipt: "It was ironic." Nobody bought it. Nobody cared much either.

situations.text: Also Sal, the bodega cat, has fallen asleep on 500 of your flyers.

choices.label: Photo op with the cat
choices.receipt: "Also Sal endorses {candidate}" (he did not). +1.

fail.receipt: Also Sal bit the photographer. Still a good picture. +0.5.

choices.label: Wait for him to move
choices.receipt: Four hours later, he moved. The team bonded over it.

choices.label: Print new flyers
choices.receipt: New flyers. Also Sal kept the old ones.

situations.text: Papa-Dani is cutting a ribbon on a fixed pothole across from your {place} rally.

choices.label: Walk over and shake his hand
choices.receipt: A handshake over a pothole. Very civic. Both of you got a bump.

choices.label: Point at the next pothole
choices.receipt: "There's another one right there, Mr. Mayor." There was. -1 for him.

fail.receipt: The crowd booed. Not him. -1 in {place}.

choices.label: Ignore him
choices.receipt: {candidate} stuck to the plan. Half the cameras did too.

situations.text: Goldcrest wants to buy The Borough Bugle. "How much is a newspaper?"

choices.label: Let him
choices.receipt: The Bugle now loves Goldcrest. Its readers noticed. +1.5, for now.

choices.label: Talk him down
choices.receipt: Goldcrest sulked for a day and bought a boat instead.

choices.label: Leak that he asked
choices.get: A funny story, Heat on him
choices.receipt: "Candidate Tried To Buy This Newspaper" ran in the newspaper. -0.5.

situations.text: A hot mic catches Goldcrest asking "who still takes the bus?"

choices.label: Put him on the Q32 tomorrow
choices.receipt: Goldcrest rode the Q32 and tapped his card wrong four times. Strangely charming.

fail.receipt: Goldcrest rode the Q32 in a car-service blazer. -1.

choices.label: Say he meant "the gondola"
choices.receipt: "He meant the gondola." Nobody believes this. Some people laughed.

choices.label: Apologize
choices.receipt: A real apology, rare for him. The clip lived anyway.

situations.text: Castellano's {place} speech is 40 minutes long. It's minute 22.

choices.label: Signal her to wrap up
choices.receipt: She wrapped up at minute 25. The crowd cheered, partly from relief. +1 in {place}.

choices.label: Let her finish
choices.receipt: Forty minutes. Six students took notes. Everyone else took the bus.

choices.label: Cue the music
choices.receipt: The music played her off. +1.5 in {place}. She did not speak to you all evening.

situations.text: Her former students start a "Castellano Core" trend: cardigans and charts.

choices.label: Lean in: post with them
choices.receipt: Castellano posted a chart in a cardigan. The kids lost it. +1.5.

choices.label: Let it run on its own
choices.receipt: The trend ran by itself. +0.5.

choices.label: Sell "Castellano Core" cardigans
choices.receipt: Cardigans sold out. Castellano found out from a student.

situations.text: A heckler is getting under Frankie's skin at the {place} rally.

choices.label: Let Frankie answer him
choices.receipt: Frankie answered with a story about his father's bus route. The heckler hugged him. +1.5.

fail.receipt: Frankie told the heckler where to put his sign. On camera. -1.5.

choices.label: Pull Frankie off stage
choices.receipt: Frankie came off swearing about "handlers." No incident.

choices.label: Have the crowd drown him out
choices.receipt: The crowd chanted "Ham-mer! Ham-mer!" The heckler left.

situations.text: There's a picket line outside the hall booked for Frankie's fundraiser.

choices.label: Move the fundraiser
choices.receipt: Fundraiser moved. Frankie brought the strikers coffee.

choices.label: Join the picket instead
choices.receipt: Frankie spent the fundraiser on the picket line. The photos are perfect. +2.

choices.label: Cross it
choices.receipt: Frankie crossed, grim-faced. The money's in. Something isn't.

situations.text: Kaylee wants to go live from the campaign office. Right now.

choices.label: Let her
choices.receipt: Kaylee's live hit a million viewers. +2.

fail.receipt: The whole strategy whiteboard was in frame. -1.

choices.label: Script it with her
choices.receipt: A scripted live. Kaylee ad-libbed only twice. +1.

choices.label: Take the phone
choices.receipt: Kaylee posted a black square about "creative control."

situations.text: Kaylee's tea sponsor wants a mention in every speech.

choices.label: Take the deal
choices.receipt: "This rally is brought to you by..." C$8,000 richer. -0.5.

choices.label: One mention, at the end
choices.receipt: One mention. Kaylee sipped on cue. C$3,000.

choices.label: Turn it down
choices.receipt: No tea deal. Kaylee drinks it anyway, off camera.

situations.text: Deb Okonkwo says Local 117's endorsement is "still open." Her nephew Kyle needs a job. Kyle has a podcast.

choices.label: Give Kyle a job
choices.receipt: Kyle is now "Director of Vibes." Local 117 endorsed {candidate} on the steps of the hall. +1.5.

fail.receipt: Local 117 endorsed. Then Kyle's podcast did an episode called "My No-Show Job." +0.5.

choices.label: Promise the union a seat
choices.cost: A promise you'll have to keep
choices.receipt: A seat on the transit board, in writing. Deb laminated it. +0.8.

choices.label: Just ask for it
choices.receipt: "Nobody asks anymore," Deb said. A warm maybe. +0.3.

situations.text: Auntie Joy Asante has endorsed the Mayor for 20 years. Her block party needs a C$12,000 sound system.

choices.label: Buy the sound system
choices.receipt: The speakers arrived Friday. By Saturday, the whole block was chanting {candidate}'s name. +1.5.

fail.receipt: Joy kept the speakers and kept endorsing the Mayor. They sound incredible.

choices.label: Lend her your DJ
choices.receipt: The DJ played one remix too many, but Joy danced. +0.6.

choices.label: Show up and work the grill
choices.cost: Your clothes smell like jerk chicken
choices.receipt: {candidate} grilled for four hours. Joy still likes the Mayor. She likes {candidate} more than last year. +0.3.

situations.text: Lionel Chu will move the Flushing Merchants' Guild to {candidate}: his nephew's restaurant on every flyer, and C$10,000 "for menus."

choices.label: Pay for the "menus"
choices.receipt: Every shop on Main Street put up a {candidate} poster. The menus never existed. +1.5.

choices.label: Just the flyers
choices.receipt: The dumplings look great on the flyer. Lionel says he's "thinking." +0.6.

choices.label: Say no
choices.receipt: No deal. Lionel told the Mayor, who sent him a ribbon.

situations.text: Pastor Ellis Grant says he'll "pray on" an endorsement. The church roof is C$8,000 short.

choices.label: Fix the roof, quietly
choices.receipt: New roof. Sunday's sermon was about "a candidate who keeps the rain off." +1.

choices.label: Volunteer at Sunday supper
choices.receipt: {candidate} served 200 plates. The pastor is still praying on it. +0.4.

situations.text: A precinct captain in {place} offers 300 votes at C$20 each. "Cash by Sunday. No receipts, obviously."

choices.label: Pay the C$6,000
choices.receipt: Three hundred twenties, three hundred handshakes. +3 in {place}.

fail.receipt: Two of the 300 posted their twenties. The Borough Bugle did the math. -1 in {place}.

choices.label: Pay for "rides to the polls"
choices.receipt: Forty cars, one route, every rider wearing your button. +1.5 in {place}.

choices.label: Knock doors instead
choices.receipt: Twelve floors, no elevator, eighty promises. +0.8 in {place}.

situations.text: A bodega in {place} offers a free sandwich for every "I Voted for {candidate}" photo. On your tab: C$3,500.

choices.label: A sandwich per vote photo
choices.receipt: The line went around the block. Every photo had a sandwich in it. +2 in {place}.

fail.receipt: Turns out paying for votes in sandwiches is still paying for votes. The Bugle ran the photos. +0.5 in {place}.

choices.label: Sandwiches for everyone
choices.receipt: Free lunch, no strings. {place} noticed. +1.

choices.label: No sandwiches
choices.receipt: No sandwiches. The bodega cat turned its back on {candidate}.

situations.text: Your field team found a few hundred absentee ballots for voters who moved away, or died. "They'd want to vote for us."

choices.label: Fill them in
choices.receipt: Some very loyal voters in {place}, considering. +3.5.

fail.receipt: Mrs. Dombrowski, who died in 2019, voted twice. Her grandson noticed. -2 in {place}.

choices.label: Shred them
choices.cost: The ballots, and a little sleep
choices.receipt: Shredded. The office smells like guilt and toner.

choices.label: Hand them to the Board
choices.receipt: {candidate} turned the ballots in. A local news crew called it "refreshing." +0.5.

situations.text: A "turnout consultant" can bus in 200 voters with Queens addresses they've "recently acquired." C$9,000.

choices.label: Book the bus
choices.receipt: Two hundred very new New Yorkers voted in {place}. +2.5.

fail.receipt: The driver honked all the way down Steinway. Someone filmed the out-of-state plates. -1.5 in {place}.

choices.label: Bus seniors to early voting
choices.receipt: Forty seniors, one bus, one lunch stop that ran long. +1.2 in {place}.

situations.text: Papa-Dani's team is handing out C$20 "pothole inconvenience refunds" outside polling sites in {place}.

choices.label: Match him, twenty for twenty
choices.receipt: Two tables, two stacks of twenties, one confused electorate. +2 in {place}.

choices.label: Film it, send it to the Bugle
choices.receipt: The Bugle ran it: "Mayor's Refund Program Refunds Only Outside Polling Sites." Mayor -1.5.

choices.label: Rise above it
choices.receipt: {candidate} rose above it. {place} took the twenties. -1.

situations.text: The Borough Bugle has your campaign's secret. It runs tomorrow.

choices.label: Deny everything
choices.receipt: Denied. The story ran smaller than it could have. -1.

fail.receipt: Denied. Then the receipts came out. -3.

choices.label: Blame a cut-out
choices.receipt: "A consultant acted alone." Half the city believed it. -1.5.

choices.label: Confess and apologize
choices.receipt: {candidate} owned it. -2.5 today, and it's over.

choices.label: Counter-leak about the Mayor
choices.receipt: Two scandals, one news cycle. Everyone lost a little. The Mayor lost more.

situations.text: The Mayor's campaign offered {target} a job. Double the pay.

choices.label: Counter-offer
choices.receipt: {target} stayed, with a raise and a better chair.

choices.label: Let them go
choices.receipt: {target} cleaned out their desk. The Mayor's office sent them a ribbon.

choices.label: Poach one of his in return
choices.receipt: You hired his scheduler. He's "reviewing his calendar."

situations.text: A lawsuit lands on the campaign office. Someone wants money, or an apology.

choices.label: Settle
choices.receipt: Settled for C$5,000. Nobody's talking about it. Good.

choices.label: Fight it
choices.receipt: You fought it and won the first round. +0.5.

fail.receipt: You fought it and lost. C$6,000 in all. -1.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.receipt: Ignoring a lawsuit: C$7,000 and a headline. -1.
